title: How We Build Websites — Our Process from Kickoff to Launch
excerpt: Most agencies are vague about their process. Here's ours, step by step — what happens, in what order, and what we need from you to make it go smoothly.

blocks.text: Most agency websites have a "Process" page that says something like: discover → design → build → launch. It's not wrong. It's just not useful.
What does "discover" actually mean? Who talks to who? When do you see the first design? What if you don't like it? When do you need to hand over your copy? What happens after launch?
This post answers those questions for a standard webvise project. By the end, you'll know exactly what to expect — and what we'll need from you.
The Full Process at a Glance
Here's the full sequence from kick-off to live site, with rough timings for a standard business site (5–30 pages):

rows: Map requirements, audience, goals, and content
Visual concept, desktop + mobile layouts, feedback loop
Full site in Next.js, content integration, forms, SEO
Client review, revisions, cross-device and cross-browser testing

blocks.text: Total: 3–4 weeks from kick-off to live. Larger or more complex projects take longer — we'll scope that before starting.
Phase 1: Discovery
What we do

Before a single pixel is designed, we need to understand what you're building and why. Discovery is a focused 60–90 minute call (or an asynchronous brief for clients who prefer it) where we work through:

items: Your business, your audience, and the job this website needs to do
The pages and content types you need (services, blog, case studies, contact, etc.)
Your existing brand: logo, colours, typography, tone of voice
Sites you like — and why. Sites you don't like — and why.
Technical requirements: forms, integrations, analytics, existing domain setup
Launch constraints: hard deadlines or events you're building toward

blocks.text: What you provide
For discovery, you need: your brand assets (logo file, ideally SVG or high-res PNG), any existing copy you want to keep, and access to your current website analytics if you have them.
Output
A written brief and sitemap you approve before we move to design. After this, there's no ambiguity about scope.
Phase 2: Design
What we do
We design in the browser — not just static mockups. You'll see live, responsive layouts on real devices, not Figma frames that don't show you how a section scrolls or how the mobile nav behaves.

We deliver one strong direction based on the brief. Not three vague options to pick from — one well-considered proposal with clear rationale for the decisions we made. This is faster and produces better outcomes than option overload.
The revision process

The first design review is a call or async walkthrough where you tell us what's working and what isn't. We collect feedback, revise, and return. Standard projects include two rounds of design revision. If the discovery brief was thorough, we rarely need more than one.
What you provide

Your final copy for the main pages needs to be ready before we move into build. Not perfect — but content you're happy with. The site is structured around your words. Placeholder text creates real problems downstream.
Phase 3: Build
What we do
Once design is approved, we build the full site in Next.js. This is where the designs become real — connected to your actual content, fully responsive, optimised for performance from day one.
We handle:

items: Full Next.js development with TypeScript
All pages from the approved sitemap
Contact forms and other forms, connected to your email or CRM
Analytics integration (Google Analytics, PostHog, or similar)
Image optimisation: WebP conversion, lazy loading, responsive sizing
On-page SEO: meta titles, descriptions, Open Graph tags, structured data
Performance optimisation: static generation, CDN deployment on Vercel

blocks.text: What you provide during build

Final copy for all pages. Any photography or imagery you own the rights to — we can source stock imagery if needed. Access to any integrations you need connected: Google Analytics property ID, form recipient email address, CRM API keys.
Staging environment
You have access to a password-protected staging URL from day one of build. You can check progress at any time — you won't wait until everything is "done" to see it.
Phase 4: Review & QA
What we do
Before asking you to sign off, we run an internal QA pass covering:

items: Cross-browser testing: Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge
Mobile testing: iPhone (Safari), Android (Chrome), tablet
Form testing: submissions reach the right inbox, confirmation emails fire
Analytics verification: events and pageviews tracking correctly
PageSpeed audit: 90+ target on both mobile and desktop
Broken link check
Spelling and grammar review across all pages

blocks.text: Client review

After our internal QA, you get a structured review session on staging. We walk through every page. You mark up feedback directly on the staging site or send a consolidated feedback document. We process revisions and return for final sign-off before scheduling launch.
Phase 5: Launch
What we do
Launch is the DNS cutover: pointing your domain from your old host to Vercel. It happens in minutes, but we prepare carefully:

items: We lower DNS TTL 24–48 hours before launch to minimise switchover delay
We configure all 301 redirects for any URLs that changed during the project
We verify analytics and form submissions are working on production before announcing
We check Core Web Vitals post-launch using PageSpeed Insights
We monitor the site for the first 24 hours after cutover

blocks.text: What about downtime?

A DNS cutover is not taking the site offline. Your old site stays live until the new one is resolving globally — typically 15–60 minutes. Visitors see your old site during the transition, then your new one. No gap in service.
Phase 6: After Launch
First week

We monitor Core Web Vitals, error rates, and crawl behavior for the first 7 days. If anything unexpected comes up — an edge case we didn't catch in QA, a layout issue on a specific device — we fix it at no extra cost.
Handover

We document what was built: page structure, how to add new content, what's deployed where. If you have an in-house developer taking over maintenance, we walk them through the codebase. If you're managing it yourself, we walk you through the update process.
Ongoing support — the managed retainer

Most of our clients stay on a managed editing retainer after launch. It works like this: email us changes in plain language — "update the pricing on the services page", "add this new team member", "publish this blog post" — and we handle it. Most updates are processed automatically within minutes. Larger structural changes are handled manually within 24–48 hours.
The retainer starts at €25/month. No contract — cancel any time.
What You Need to Provide — and When
Projects run smoothly when clients are responsive and have their content ready. Here's a checklist:
Before kick-off

items: Logo file (SVG preferred, high-res PNG acceptable)
Brand guidelines if you have them (colours, typography, tone of voice)
Access to your current site's analytics
Examples of sites you like, with notes on what appeals to you
A list of the pages you need

blocks.text: Before design sign-off

items: Feedback on the design within 48–72 hours of delivery
A clear decision-maker — one person with final sign-off authority

blocks.text: Before build starts

items: Final copy for all main pages: header, hero, services, about, contact
Any photography or imagery you want to use
Integration credentials: Google Analytics property ID, form email address, CRM API keys if applicable

blocks.text: How Long Does It Actually Take?
Timeline depends on two things: project complexity and how quickly you respond. Here's what to expect:
The single biggest source of delay in any project is waiting for client feedback or content. If you're available and your content is ready, we move fast.
Common Questions About Our Process
What if I don't have copy ready?

We can write it — copywriting is available as an add-on. The alternative is using placeholder text during build and swapping in real copy before launch, but this always takes longer than clients expect. We recommend having at least a first draft ready when build starts.
Can I request changes after launch?
Yes — that's exactly what the managed retainer is for. For clients not on a retainer, we quote individual change requests as they come in.
Do I own the code?
Yes. Everything we build is yours. After launch, you have full access to the GitHub repository and can hire any developer to work on it.
What platform does the site run on?
We deploy on Vercel. The free tier handles most business sites without issue. If you grow beyond those limits, Vercel's paid plans start at €20/month.
Ready to Start?

If you know what you want to build, book a free 20-minute call at [webvise.io/contact](/#contact). We'll talk through the scope, give you a fixed-price quote, and you'll know exactly what you're getting before we start.

If you have a WordPress site and are considering a migration specifically, get a free WordPress Health Report at [webvise.io/wp-health-report](/wp-health-report). It shows your current performance scores and what they'd look like after a migration to Next.js.
